newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Officials of the Department of Foreign Affairs yesterday voiced concern over reports that the Indonesian government was preventing some 30 Filipino geologists and mining engineers from coming home in view of the Busang gold mine scandal.

- The 18 Chinese fishermen arrested by the Navy for poaching in Philippine waters were charged with illegal entry and will be held indefinitely, Foreign Affairs Secretary Domingo Siazon said yesterday.
- President Fidel Ramos left yesterday on a ten-day mission to Mexico and Panama to strengthen "old and close historical ties" and pursue his administration's economic diplomacy.

- The Philippine Central Bank disputed yesterday projections by some analysts that the economy was headed toward a financial crisis such as Thailand's, saying there were "fundamental differences" between the two emerging Southeast Asian nations.
- The newly-resuscitated Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank will reopen tomorrow as scheduled under its new owners led by the Keppel Group of Singapore.
- Share prices yesterday racked up gains for the second day in a row but many market watchers remained unconvinced the bourse had touched bottom after the thrashing last week.
